title: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword

nodes.name: Third-person game camera setup and obstruction handling
nodes.purpose: Starting camera pose, named camera contexts loaded from data, camera source priority and the sphere push-out used to keep the lens out of walls. The per-update follow logic is still a stub in this repository.

nodes.name: Lock-on and interaction target manager
nodes.purpose: Keeps a small ranked pool of things the player can lock onto or interact with, and defines the preset prompt shapes for pick up, catch, talk and read.

nodes.name: Remote flying beetle gadget
nodes.purpose: Throwable flying drone with a timed flight, upgrade tiers, collision spheres and grab or bounce reactions. The steering update itself is not decompiled.

nodes.name: Bomb actor: rolling, fuse, blast and bomb flower
nodes.purpose: Throwable bomb with slope rolling, bounce, sinking, a swelling fuse, a timed blast sphere and a regrowing bomb flower variant.

nodes.name: Arrow and slingshot projectile actor
nodes.purpose: One projectile actor serves bow arrows and slingshot pellets: damage tiers, straight flight then drop, water entry, ricochet, sticking and pickup.

nodes.name: Flying enemy AI: bat swarm and sky serpent
nodes.purpose: State-machine AI for a small bat enemy that dozes, wakes, chases and dives, and for a large sky serpent that escorts and lunges at the flying mount.

nodes.name: Skittish ground creature AI
nodes.purpose: Small creature that walks, runs and flees from the player, with gravity and distance thresholds that decide when it escapes or gets cornered.

nodes.name: Boss sword beam projectile
nodes.purpose: Straight-flying beam with two capsule hitboxes, ground hover, impact vanish and a return routine that sends a deflected beam back toward the player.

nodes.name: Flying bird mount base
nodes.purpose: Shared base for bird actors: glide, flap and dive pose selection from the heading pitch, and a ray fan that finds an escape direction after a collision. Player-driven flight states are empty stubs.

nodes.name: Actor versus level collision
nodes.purpose: Ground, roof and wall resolution for actors against level geometry using downward probes, roof probes and swept line checks.

nodes.name: Attack, target and body collision scheduler
nodes.purpose: Per-update pass that collects attack, target and body shapes and resolves them. The resolution bodies are empty in this repository, so only the schedule is mapped.

nodes.name: Weighted loot drop tables
nodes.purpose: Rolls a percent-based drop from a numbered table, filters entries by what the player owns, and spawns the items in a fan.

nodes.name: Catchable critter reactions
nodes.purpose: Shared base for small catchable creatures: scare checks from player speed and rolling, bug net reaction and death rules.

nodes.name: Sword swing trail ribbon
nodes.purpose: Ring buffer of blade edge samples that fade over time and draw as a translucent triangle strip.

cards.name: Camera start pose behind the player
cards.summary: On creation the camera aims at a point above the player, sits on a short boom behind the facing direction and uses a moderate field of view.
cards.behavior: The look-at point is the player position raised by a fixed height. The camera position is that point plus a polar offset with a fixed length, a fixed upward angle and a yaw that points opposite to the player facing, so the first frame looks over the shoulder. The field of view is set once here. The per-update follow logic for the chase, lock-on and other handlers is a stub in this repository, so only this start pose is confirmed. Treat the numbers as a good default for a third-person follow camera.

constants.name: start boom elevation angle (second polar argument, read as pitch)
start boom yaw offset from player facing

cards.name: Named camera contexts loaded from data
cards.summary: Camera behavior is chosen by name from a data file, with thirteen handler slots in code, so each movement mode can own its own framing.
cards.behavior: A camera parameter file is read at start-up and holds float tables, flag tables, styles and named trends. Code caches the index of each trend by name, including swim, surface, dive, sky dive, parachute, crawl, rope, tightrope, bird ride, the gadget beetle, claw shot, cannon, town, dungeon and field. A lookup that fails falls back to the first trend, and a style lookup returns minus one. The thirteen handler slots in the table (chase, lock-on and others) have empty bodies here, so only the naming scheme and the data-driven design are confirmed. Use it as a checklist of contexts that each deserve a distinct framing in a third-person game.

cards.name: Camera push-out from walls and obstructions
cards.summary: The camera tests a thick line to the player, steps a point back along the ray when blocked, and pushes a probe sphere out of level planes.
cards.behavior: An obstruction line test uses a fixed radius and ignores the player and the actor the player controls. A point version repeats up to ten times: each pass moves the test end back toward the start by a short step along the ray, then returns the last blocked point. A separate sphere pass loops a tuned number of times. Each pass collects every level plane that the sphere overlaps and accepts a plane only when the camera focus point is not behind it by more than a small slack. It keeps the largest positive and the largest negative push per axis, adds them, normalizes the sum and scales it by the deepest penetration, plus a small extra margin so the sphere ends just clear. A final pass applies the largest push per axis. The tuned loop count lives in a tuning struct whose value is not in the source.

constants.name: point push-out maximum passes
constants.unit: passes per update (30 Hz inferred, unverified)

cards.name: Camera region source priority
cards.summary: The active camera comes from a forced id, an override with priority, a stored region id, or the room default, in that order.
cards.behavior: A forced camera request wins over everything and is tagged with the highest kind code. An override request only replaces the stored one when its priority is at least the stored priority, and it is tagged with a lower kind code; a flag chooses between two override kinds. After those, a third stored id is checked, and last comes the room default camera. A separate ground probe reads the camera region id that is stored on the polygon under the actor, with its own result for the water surface. The probe starts a little above the actor, uses a crawl position copy while crawling, and counts a player in water, riding, hanging or on vines as grounded for camera purposes. The code that copies the probe result into the third stored id is not decompiled here.

constants.name: ground probe lift above the actor
swim camera ground margin above feet

capabilities: swim and crawl camera special cases

cards.name: Lock-on candidate pool and facing score
cards.summary: A fixed pool of eight ranked targets per group, apparently double buffered, plus a score that prefers targets in front of the player.
cards.behavior: There are five groups of candidates, each with two pools that look like a double buffer. A pool holds at most eight entries sorted by a stored rank value, highest first. A new entry that outranks an existing one is inserted at that slot, and when the pool is full the last entry is dropped; an actor that is already present under the same key is rejected. The facing score takes the absolute difference between the player heading and the direction to the target, normalized so 1 equals a half turn. A target within 90 degrees of the heading scores from 0.25 at dead ahead up to 0.5 at the side, so lower is better. A target behind the side line scores by the raw fraction, from 0.5 up to 1. Which value feeds the sort rank is not decompiled here, and the lock-on button checks are stubs.

constants.name: angle normalization, numerator over 65536
constants.unit: normalized units per full angle range

cards.name: Interaction prompt presets and reach values
cards.summary: Objects register prompts through preset shapes for pick up, catch, talk, examine and read, then pass their own reach and vertical window.
cards.behavior: Each preset is a table of numbers keyed by an interaction kind. Callers copy the preset, then overwrite a reach value and a lower and upper vertical bound. A bomb offers a short pick-up reach, a bomb flower offers a longer prompt reach with a wide vertical window, and a catchable critter offers a long catch reach with an equal window up and down. The pick-up preset itself carries a smaller asymmetric window. The meaning of each table slot is named only by offset in the source, so the reach and window roles here are inferred from the argument names the callers pass.

constants.name: pick-up preset vertical window upper bound

cards.name: Beetle gadget flight timer and warning flash
cards.summary: The drone flies for a time set by the player upgrade, then flashes faster in three stages and plays a warning sound at each peak.
cards.behavior: On launch the drone takes its speed and flight time from player-stat getters (not decompiled here), sets its pitch to a bias minus a player pitch value, and records the launch point lifted by a fixed height. A remaining-time value can only be lowered, never raised, by later requests. Once the remaining time drops under the warning time, a flash timer counts down. The flash period is long while the timer is high, medium in the middle and short at the end. Each period starts at full red on the update that plays the warning sound, then the tint falls linearly and stays dark for the last few updates before the next period. The upgrade tiers swap the pincers, body and wings models by tier comparison. The steering update for the Move state is empty in this repository.

constants.name: launch counter, source remark equals 1.5 seconds
dark updates at the start of each flash period
launch pitch bias
constants.unit: angle units, 65536 per full turn, applied per update (30 Hz inferred, unverified)

cards.name: Beetle gadget collision, bounce-off and grab
cards.summary: The drone owns two spheres and a wall circle; a hit either grabs a light object with the hook upgrade or reverses the drone away from the target.
cards.behavior: The attack sphere radius is a fixed small value for the first sphere. The second sphere radius and the wall circle radius are replaced at creation by a player-stat getter, so cite that getter and not the table default. The ground clearance and roof clearance are fixed. On an attack hit, a target flagged as grabbable is taken when the hook upgrade is owned and the drone is moving, but the grab routine body is a stub here. Otherwise a hit that is not a bonk starts the cancel state: the rebound direction is the horizontal vector from the target to the drone, falling back to the reverse of the drone heading when the two overlap exactly, scaled by the horizontal speed, with the vertical component inverted and then normalized. A bonk plays the pincer animation and starts a rumble, at most once per update. A bomb grabbed by the drone gets a short grace period before contact detonation.

constants.name: first attack sphere radius (second sphere radius is a player getter)

capabilities: grab small objects with an upgrade

cards.name: Bomb rolling on slopes
cards.summary: A thrown bomb rolls as a sphere, speeds down slopes steeper than a threshold, and loses speed by small fixed steps on flat ground.
cards.behavior: The bomb is a sphere with a fixed base radius times its scale. While on ground the vertical speed is reduced by the horizontal speed times the sine of the slope along the travel direction, and horizontal speed is scaled by the cosine. On slopes at or above the roll angle the bomb adds a push down the slope, multiplies speed by a damping factor each update and clamps speed to a cap; on flatter ground the speed chases zero by a step. The step is largest for a plain slide, small while rolling after a throw, and in between while rolling on soft sand. After a throw the velocity blends the throw heading and the ordinary heading with a weight equal to the roll timer times a factor, clamped to one. The timer starts at sixty and only counts down on ground, so the throw heading keeps full weight for about ten updates and then fades over fifty. The visual spin rate makes the surface move without slipping: distance divided by circumference times a full turn. Gravity and terminal speed come from player-stat getters that are not decompiled. The Wait update and the main update are marked as not matching the original bytes, so details may differ slightly.

cards.name: Bomb bounce, sinking and water loss
cards.summary: Bombs bounce off steep walls and slopes, lose speed on landing, sink slowly in sand, fast in cursed water and disappear in water.
cards.behavior: A wall bounce triggers when the wall angle differs from the travel heading by more than about 95 degrees and the horizontal speed is above one unit per update; it mirrors the heading and scales speed by a player-stat bounce factor. A ground landing on a slope of fifty degrees or more, with enough speed and a heading toward the slope, also bounces off the slope normal. On every landing the fall speed becomes a bounce speed scaled by the same bounce factor. If the bomb is not rolling and that bounce is under a stop threshold, or the surface is sand or cursed water, horizontal speed instead drains by a fixed step per update. Otherwise horizontal speed is damped and the bounce is capped by a player-stat maximum. A landing harder than a threshold plays a bounce sound. In cursed water the sink target is deep and the sink rate equals the fall speed, and in sand the target is shallow at a slow rate; reaching the deep limit deletes the bomb. Entering real water halves speed, shrinks the bomb to nothing at a fixed rate and deletes it, and the fuse stops.

constants.unit: angle units, 65536 per full turn, applied per update (30 Hz inferred, unverified)

cards.name: Bomb fuse swell, blast sphere and bomb flower
cards.summary: The fuse flashes faster in halving stages and swells in the last updates, the blast is a short-lived hit sphere, and a flower regrows its bomb.
cards.behavior: The fuse length comes from a player-stat getter. It counts down only while the bomb is free: not on a flower, not carried by the player, not in water. A bomb explodes when the fuse ends, when something hits it, when a burning player touches it, when it touches lava, or when a grabbed bomb loses contact after its grace period. The flash interval shrinks in halving stages as the fuse falls under half of the previous stage. Within each interval the tint falls from near full to zero, stays at zero for the last few updates, and then jumps back to full. In the last few updates the model swells by a growing step with a cap. The blast is one sphere set at the bomb position with a radius from a player-stat getter, except a crawl-space flower bomb that uses a larger fixed radius. The sphere is refreshed for three more updates and then the actor is deleted. A blast hitting another bomb chains it. A bomb flower starts tiny and grows by a fixed step per update until full size, then offers a pick-up prompt. Rumble depends on the squared distance to the player. The checkExplode and Wait functions are marked as not matching the original bytes.

constants.name: swell window at the end of the fuse
swell growth is remaining updates below the window divided by this
flash zero-tint window at the end of each interval
blast sphere refresh stops when the counter passes this value
flower regrow step
constants.unit: scale per update (30 Hz inferred, unverified)

cards.name: Arrow flight, drop and damage tiers
cards.summary: Arrows fly straight for a draw-dependent distance, then fall under a small constant gravity; damage depends on bow type and a full-charge bonus.
cards.behavior: Damage comes from a four-entry table indexed by the current bow type; index zero is the default stored in the attack descriptor. A fully charged shot multiplies damage by a bonus and rounds. On launch the velocity and the straight-flight distance come from player-stat getters that are not decompiled. While the arrow is inside that distance it moves in a straight line and tests a swept capsule along a segment that reaches a fixed length plus one step ahead of the tip. Past the distance, each update adds a constant downward gravity, recomputes pitch from velocity, and counts down a lifetime before despawn. The capsule radius is small and grows for long flights: after the arrow has flown beyond one distance it rises linearly up to a bonus at a second distance (the header annotations give one thousand, four thousand and fifty). Six launch slots are tracked so arrows stuck in the world are removed once six newer arrows have been fired. The launch function is marked as not matching the original bytes.

constants.name: arrow gravity
constants.unit: world units per update squared (30 Hz inferred, unverified)

constants.name: launch slots before an old arrow is removed
radius growth starts after this flight distance (header annotation)
radius growth ends at this flight distance (header annotation)

cards.name: Arrow ricochet, sticking, water and pickup
cards.summary: Arrows ricochet off shields and hard surfaces, stick in soft ones, slow in water, and can be picked up again from where they stuck.
cards.behavior: A hit on a shield or on a hard surface class puts the arrow in a bound state: it flies backward with a random speed and spin, falls under its own gravity, reflects off planes at half speed with halved spin, and despawns when it settles on the ground or falls far below its start. Other surface classes stick the arrow and clamp the embed angle to a fixed limit. A stuck arrow wobbles with a quadratically decaying amount and grows a small pick-up sphere; touching it with a bow owned gives one arrow back. Stuck arrows stay until six newer arrows have been fired or the surface they hold to goes away. Entering water sets a slower velocity and shortens the look-ahead. A shot that is deeper than a fixed depth under the surface shrinks away and despawns, and one that rises far above the surface despawns at once. The despawn flag is followed by a short delay before deletion.

cards.name: Slingshot pellets and eight-pellet scattershot
cards.summary: The same actor serves slingshot shots with a bigger sweep radius, stronger gravity and instant despawn on hit; a full charge adds a ring of eight pellets.
cards.behavior: Slingshot pellets use a larger sweep radius than arrows. After their straight distance they fall faster than arrows and their horizontal speed is pulled toward a cap by a fixed step (the header annotates both values). A pellet that hits any surface or enemy plays a small impact effect and despawns; it never sticks or ricochets, and it despawns on entering water. Its attack descriptor has a damage of zero and carries only its attack type tag. A fully charged shot spawns eight extra pellets of a special type. Each is rotated about the aim axis by an equal ring step plus random jitter, and is offset from the aim by a cone angle from a player-stat getter minus a random trim, so the pellets scatter as a ring. The launch function is marked as not matching the original bytes.

cards.name: Bat enemy chase, hover offset and dive
cards.summary: The bat eases toward a hover point around the player, rerolls that point every few updates, then dives with a hit sphere that turns on after a short delay.
cards.behavior: In chase the bat picks a hover offset relative to the player with a random side, height and depth, and rerolls it every ten to nineteen updates. The depth range differs depending on whether the bat is behind the player, meaning the direction from the bat to the player lies within 90 degrees of the player heading. The bat position eases toward the hover point by a tenth of the remaining distance per update, limited by a speed that ramps up toward a cap. Yaw and pitch turn toward the target through a divisor and a per-update angle limit, and pitch turns far slower than yaw. When the player is within a horizontal range but the bat has not reached its hover point, a random countdown of twenty to thirty-nine updates leads to the dive state. In the dive the contact hit sphere switches on after eight updates and the bat then returns to chase. When both the player and the hover point are near, the bat switches to a hover state if it is behind the player or the player is mid-action. It gives up and goes idle when it leaves a leash circle around its home. The body sphere radius and the attack descriptor damage are fixed values.

constants.name: chase speed cap
constants.unit: world units per update (30 Hz inferred, unverified)

cards.name: Bat enemy dozing, waking and idle roaming
cards.summary: The bat sleeps until the player is near and visible, wakes after a short eye-open delay, then roams between random waypoints around its home.
cards.behavior: While dozing the bat checks every ten to fourteen updates for the player inside a fixed radius with a clear line, and arms a short random wake timer. Once the timer passes a closing threshold the eye animation plays, and at zero the bat enters the wake state. Some bats also wake on a long random timer counted in seconds. In roam the bat picks a waypoint around its start with a wider horizontal than vertical spread and flies there at a low cruise speed. A periodic home-radius check also sets an actor property flag, but what that flag changes is outside this file.

cards.name: Sky serpent escort and lunge attack run
cards.summary: A large flying enemy roams, closes in on the player mount, flies in formation, then lunges in staged distance bands with a long body of sphere hitboxes.
cards.behavior: Three sphere sizes cover head, spine and rear. In random move the target is a point near its birth point and the speed target is a base value scaled by a small random factor. In move the target is derived from the bird mount; at a far horizontal distance it steers toward the mount, and inside a nearer horizontal distance it enters the front attack state. The front attack uses full three-dimensional distance, not horizontal distance, with bands from far to close: the first sets a hold timer from distance divided by speed, the second plays the lunge sound, and the third starts a longer hold. The parallel state flies in formation offsets around the mount, then lunges at a speed of at least a fixed value with a short hit window and a weak homing that blends heading toward the mount by a small ratio per update. The attack ends early when the hit sphere touches the bird or the player. Turning uses a divisor and a turn step that grows by a fixed amount each update toward a random target. If the serpent is outside the camera view it falls back to the formation state.

cards.name: Skittish creature run, escape and dash
cards.summary: A small ground creature walks or runs normally, flees when the player comes close, and dashes straight away when frightened by a threat.
cards.behavior: A frightened creature inside a trigger radius switches from run to escape, otherwise it only walks. Escape sets a stronger gravity and a speed target eased by a ratio and a minimum step, and it returns to walking once it is far enough from the target and no bomb is near. It stops fleeing and becomes scared when one of two blockage checks fires: a heading check and a probe of a short distance ahead, whose exact meaning is not named in the source. The dash variant first turns directly away from the player at a limited turn per update, and only then accelerates to a higher speed target; a probe of a wider distance ends the dash. Its body sphere has a fixed radius and an attack descriptor with a small damage value.

cards.name: Bird mount glide, flap and dive pose rules
cards.summary: The mount switches between glide, flap and dive poses from its heading pitch with hysteresis, and probes six or more directions to escape a wall, ground or roof hit.
cards.behavior: While gliding the bird flaps after a random interval of about one hundred to two hundred updates, or enters a dive transition when the vertical component of its heading vector (named only by offset in the source) drops under a threshold. Leaving the dive pose needs the vertical component to rise above a higher threshold, and a transition in progress can reverse earlier at an even higher one, which gives hysteresis. Pose changes use a short animation blend. After a collision flag is seen, the bird tests rays of very long length in a fixed order: up and down when it is on the ground, then left and right of its heading, then up and down again, and takes the first free direction as its avoid direction. Hit checks run every twenty to twenty-nine updates, with a sixty-update cooldown after a real hit. The player-controlled flight states of the main bird are empty stubs here.

constants.name: escape ray quarter turn
constants.unit: angle units, 65536 per full turn, applied per update (30 Hz inferred, unverified)

cards.name: Actor ground, roof and wall resolution
cards.summary: Each actor probes down from above its feet, probes up for a roof, then sweeps a line from the old to the new position at each wall height and slides out along the hit plane.
cards.behavior: The ground probe starts above the feet by the default lift minus the actor ground-up setting, and is lowered under a detected roof. When ground is found, the actor is moved up to the ground height plus the ground-up setting if that exceeds a stored threshold, vertical speed is cleared when the flag is on, and found, landing and ground-away flags are updated. A roof probe starts just under the actor position and clamps the actor under the roof by a clearance. With the line-down option, a tight floor and roof place the actor halfway between them. Walls use one swept line per wall circle: the end of the line is the new position raised by the wall height; the sample height is clamped between roof and ground at the old position; a hit moves the position to the hit point and pushes it out by the unit plane normal if the plane is not ground-like. A falling player extends the sweep by the fall speed. When no custom height is set, a sphere pass uses most of the smaller of the ground-up and roof clearance as its radius. A moving platform carries the actor before the probes. No ground is a huge negative height and no roof a huge positive one.

constants.name: default ground probe lift above feet
sphere radius fraction of the smaller clearance

capabilities: swept wall slide by plane normal

cards.name: Attack, target and body hit layers schedule
cards.summary: Hit detection splits shapes into attack, target and body layers and runs one fixed pass order each update; the bodies of the passes are not decompiled.
cards.behavior: Each object registers shapes into three lists: attack volumes, target volumes that can be hurt, and body volumes that push other bodies away. A per-update move runs these steps in order: drop dead objects, compute the broad-phase area, match attacks to targets, resolve body overlaps, clear the target hit marks, run post-move fixes, shift hit positions for a stage offset, and reset all counters. At most sixteen broad-phase areas are stored, each with a matrix and its inverse. Shapes include sphere, capsule, cylinder and triangle types. Attack type tags such as sword, bomb, arrow, slingshot, wind and bug net decide who can hurt whom, and many actors list the tags they ignore. The resolution functions are empty in this repository, so use the order and layering as design guidance.

cards.name: Percent loot roll with ownership filters
cards.summary: A drop table is a list of entries with percent weights; the roll is a one-hundred-sided random value with a gate that thins out low weights.
cards.behavior: A defeated object names a table. The roll picks a random integer from zero to ninety-nine and walks the entries, accumulating weights; the first entry whose running total exceeds the roll wins. When the walk reaches an entry with weight 15 or lower, it divides thirty by the weight, caps the result at three, and ends the whole roll with no drop unless the roll is divisible by that result. That makes rare entries rarer than the table suggests, and it can also veto rolls that would have reached later entries. Weights are zeroed for arrows before a bow is owned, seeds before a slingshot, bombs before the bomb bag, and hearts on the harder mode except for one special table. Some entries drop several items, which fan out over a half circle centered on the direction from the drop toward the player, with small random jitter. Medals owned by the player add extra heart or rupee rolls, and four tables swap to a replacement table when health is under a quarter. The source marks the spawn function as a rough, unmatched starting point.
capabilities: mercy drops when health is low

cards.name: Critter scare radii, net reaction and death rules
cards.summary: Small creatures flee from a player who rolls near them or runs close, react to the start and end of a net swing, and die in water, lava or to attacks.
cards.behavior: A scare triggers when the player is rolling and within a medium radius, or moving faster than one unit per update within a smaller radius. A creature also bolts when the player is inside its notice radius. A separate speed level reads zero when nearly still, one when under ten units per update, and two when faster; subclasses supply the notice radius for each level. Player height must be within a fixed band. A net swing counter increases while the player swings inside the notice area; the creature also bolts when the swing ends, or when the swing lasts longer than three updates. Water at the creature height and lava landings kill it, and falling far under its spawn deletes it. A set of attack types, including sword, bomb, arrow, slingshot, whip and claw shot, kills it once a short grace timer is over. A bug net hit marks it caught.

cards.name: Boss sword beam flight and return
cards.summary: A boss beam flies at a fixed speed with a thin damaging capsule and a wider deflectable capsule, vanishes on impact and can be sent back at the player.
cards.behavior: The beam heads horizontally at the player at creation. It moves in a straight line at a fixed speed. Two capsules follow it: a thin one deals damage and cannot be hit, and a wider one cannot deal damage but can be hit by the sword. The beam hovers a fixed height over the ground by a ground-up setting that differs by variant, and any ground, wall or water hit, or a damaging hit that is not reflected by a shield, ends it in one update. One special attack type on the wide capsule destroys it; other hit types on that capsule are not handled in the decompiled code. A return routine re-aims the beam at the player on the horizontal plane, enlarges its shadow radius and makes the wide capsule untargetable for ten updates so it cannot be destroyed at once. The capsule length is a fixed value times the actor scale.

cards.name: Weapon swing trail ribbon
cards.summary: Each frame the blade adds one pair of edge points to a ring buffer; every pair fades and the whole ring draws as one translucent strip.
cards.behavior: The trail has a fixed capacity chosen at creation. Each sample stores two world points and two colors, with a lifetime of one. The ring head advances on every add and the live count grows until the capacity is reached. Each update subtracts the elapsed amount from every live lifetime and removes entries at zero; when all have expired the head resets. Drawing walks the entries from newest to oldest and emits two vertices per entry as a triangle strip with alpha equal to the color alpha times the lifetime. A textured version steps the texture coordinate by a scale per entry. Blending is standard alpha, depth test on, depth write off and no culling, so the ribbon is visible from both sides.
